test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 27 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In Mendel's experiments, crossing a pea plant bearing yellow-coloured peas with a plant bearing green-coloured peas gave plants that all had yellow-coloured peas. If these plants were allowed to self-pollinate and 500 peas were collected from them, how many would be green-coloured?
solution:
The correct answer is **"Around 110".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **F1 generation is the first one. 100% yellow, then yellow(Y) is dominant trait and green(y) is recessive trait.**
 
• F2 generation results from the crossing of F1 individuals (Yy).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a09ec7ccf1e6e013201ad15dbc3b62db577204dccf37ab7b741048288fe3b224.png] 

 
• We receive **3 yellow plants and 1 green plant in the F2 generation.**
 
• Therefore, there are three yellow and one green in this F2 generation.
 
• We pronounce it as 3:1.
 
• So, No. of green plants in pea plants are, 500times{1over4}=125
 
• As **the above value is an experimental one. So, around 110 pea plants are green in actuality.**
